trading in the Equity Shares nor regarding the price at which the Equity Shares will be traded after listing.

1. Summary of the primary business
a. Business Overview - Products and Services
We are an environmental technology company offering efficient technologies and comprehensive engineering 
solutions in the field of wastewater treatment (“WWT”), wastewater recycling & reuse (“WRR”) and solid 
waste treatment (“SWT”).
b. Industries Served and Typical Customers
We primarily operate in the fields of WWT and WRR, wherein our primary customers are EPC companies who 
bid for STP projects / WRR projects, serving ultimately municipalities and government agencies that award 
these projects, and in the field of SWT, wherein our primary customers include Goa Waste Management 
Corporation and oil marketing companies.

2. Summary of the Industry (Source: F&S Report)
The global water and wastewater treatment market stood at USD 880 billion in CY2024 and expanded to USD 
934.0 billion in CY2025. The market is projected to grow to USD 1,240.0 billion by CY2030E, reflecting a 
CAGR of approximately 5.8% between CY2025 and CY2030E. The global tertiary treatment market was 
valued at USD 1.15 Bn in CY2020 and grew to USD 1.40 Bn in CY2024. It is projected to reach USD 1.94 Bn

in CY2026E and is forecasted to expand significantly to USD 4.34 Bn by CY2031F, registering a robust CAGR 
of 17.47% from CY2026E to CY2031F. The municipal solid waste management sector in India has evolved 
with rapid urbanization, rising waste generation, and increasing emphasis on scientific waste collection, 
segregation, processing, and disposal. Based on the latest municipal solid waste generation, collection and 
processing levels and the corresponding assumptions for waste conversion, energy recovery and realisation 
from recovered products, the revenue potential from these municipal solid waste-related businesses is estimated 
at approximately INR 217.4 billion in FY2026. The revenue potential is estimated to increase to approximately 
INR 329.2 billion by FY2031E, representing a CAGR of approximately 8.7% during FY2026–FY2031E.
For further information, see “Industry Overview” beginning on page 208 of the Red Herring Prospectus.
3. Promoters 
The Promoters of our Company are Sandeep Sudhakar Asolkar, Priya Sandeep Asolkar, Prachiti Sandeep 
Asolkar and Saketchandrasingh Pratapsingh Dhandoriya.
Sandeep Sudhakar Asolkar
Sandeep Sudhakar Asolkar, is one of our Promoters and is also the Chairman and Managing Director on our 
Board. He holds a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering from Sardar Patel College of Engineering, University 
of Bombay, and has completed the Senior Management Programme from IIM Ahmedabad. He has received a 
certificate in business excellence from Columbia Business School. He has over 31 years of experience in the 
environmental engineering sector. He was previously employed with Ion Exchange (India) Limited, Hindustan 
Dorr-Oliver Limited, Gherzi Eastern Limited and Klean Environmental Consultants Private Limited. He has 
received several awards and has been recognised as Icons of Navi Mumbai by the Economic Times.
Priya Sandeep Asolkar
Priya Sandeep Asolkar, is one of our Promoters. She holds a bachelor’s degree in engineering (civil) from 
Sardar Patel College of Engineering, University of Bombay. She has previously worked with Development 
Consultants Limited as senior design engineer (civil), Sterling Engineering Consultancy Services Private 
Limited in her capacity as design engineer, N. N. Purandare Consultants as junior design engineer and with 
Atlanta Construction Co. (India) Limited as an assistant engineer. Further, she has previously provided 
engineering consultancy services as a consultant to our Company. 
Prachiti Sandeep Asolkar
Prachiti Sandeep Asolkar, is one of our Promoters and is also the Executive Director of our Company. She has 
been associated with our Company since August 1, 2023. She holds a bachelor's degree in media studies 
(communication management – advertising) from Symbiosis International University, Pune. She has also 
obtained a master of science in finance degree and a master of science in international business from Hult 
International Business School. Further, she has participated in the programme on project management held at 
the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad from October 21, 2024 to October 26, 2024.
Saketchandrasingh Pratapsingh Dhandoriya
Saketchandrasingh Pratapsingh Dhandoriya is a Promoter and an Executive Director on the Board of our 
Company. He holds a diploma in mechanical engineering from Board of Technical Examination, Maharashtra. 
He has over 25 years of experience in the environmental engineering sector. He has been associated with our 
Company since 2005 and has previously served as manager – field services with Ion Exchange (India) Limited.
For further information, see “Our Management” and “Our Promoters and Promoter Group” beginning on 
pages 367 and 392, respectively, of the Red Herring Prospectus.

2. Summary of the Industry (Source: F&S Report)
The global water and wastewater treatment market stood at USD 880 billion in CY2024 and expanded to USD 
934.0 billion in CY2025. The market is projected to grow to USD 1,240.0 billion by CY2030E, reflecting a 
CAGR of approximately 5.8% between CY2025 and CY2030E. The global tertiary treatment market was 
valued at USD 1.15 Bn in CY2020 and grew to USD 1.40 Bn in CY2024. It is projected to reach USD 1.94 Bn

in CY2026E and is forecasted to expand significantly to USD 4.34 Bn by CY2031F, registering a robust CAGR 
of 17.47% from CY2026E to CY2031F. The municipal solid waste management sector in India has evolved 
with rapid urbanization, rising waste generation, and increasing emphasis on scientific waste collection, 
segregation, processing, and disposal. Based on the latest municipal solid waste generation, collection and 
processing levels and the corresponding assumptions for waste conversion, energy recovery and realisation 
from recovered products, the revenue potential from these municipal solid waste-related businesses is estimated 
at approximately INR 217.4 billion in FY2026. The revenue potential is estimated to increase to approximately 
INR 329.2 billion by FY2031E, representing a CAGR of approximately 8.7% during FY2026–FY2031E.

accumulated losses, deferred expenditure and miscellaneous expenditure not written off, as per the Restated Consolidated 
Financial Information, but does not include reserves created out of revaluation of assets, write-back of depreciation and 
amalgamation
10) Net Debt to Equity is calculated as net debt divided by total equity.
11) Fixed Asset Turnover is calculated as revenue from operations divided by average property, plant and equipment (PP&E)
12) Cash Conversion Cycle is computed as trade receivables days plus inventory days minus trade payable days; Wherein, trade 
receivable days is calculated as average trade receivables divided by revenue from operations multiplied by 365 for financial
years, inventory days is calculated as average inventory divided by cost of goods sold multiplied by 365 for financial years 
and trade payable days is calculated as average trade payables divided by cost of goods sold multiplied by 365 for financial 
years. Rounded off to the nearest whole number. Days for three month period is calculated as 365/4.
13) Total Order Book comprises of estimated value of the unexecuted portions of existing contracts or orders (including long 
term operation & maintenance contracts/orders), as well as the estimated value of new projects supported by letters of award 
(LOAs), letters of intent (LoIs), memorandum of understanding (MoUs), or other similar commitments from our customers. 
It represents business that is considered firm or likely to fructify in the foreseeable future, based on the current status of 
customer engagement. Our Total Order Book comprises the aggregate of order book for our Wastewater Treatment, 
Wastewater Recycling & Reuse and Solid Waste Treatment segments.
14) The higher number of days for the three-month period is primarily attributable to the seasonality and cyclicality of our 
business and the lower first-quarter revenue base, and may not be indicative of the underlying annual cash conversion cycle.

plant installations, on a cumulative basis, facilitated by our Company’s technology

represents the total MLD of treatment capacity for wastewater treatment plants on a cumulative basis facilitated by our 
Company’s technology.
In respect of any period which is not a full financial year, Average Equity, PP&E is calculated as the arithmetic average of the 
closing balance of Equity, PP&E as at the end of the relevant period, and the closing balance of Equity, PP&E as at the end of 
the immediately preceding Fiscal.

1. Our revenues and operations are dependent upon technology. Failure of these technologies, failure to 
upgrade or innovate these technologies or failure to identify and develop new technologies could have an 
adverse impact on our results of operations. Our products may be displaced by newer technology and any 
inability or failure to adapt to technological developments, the evolving competitive landscape or industry 
trends could harm our business and competitiveness.

accounted for 88.22%, 84.98%, 84.34% and 87.40% of our consolidated revenue from operations in the

dependent on projects, contracts or works awarded or funded by government entities, either directly or 
through our private customers. Our revenue from operations directly or indirectly attributable to

Any reduction or termination in such projects or adverse change in government policies could adversely 
affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. 
3. We derive a significant part of our revenue from our top 10 customers and we do not have long term 
contracts with most of these customers. If one or more of such customers choose not to source their

requirements from us or to terminate our long-term contracts, our business, results of operations and 
financial condition may be adversely affected.

organizations, such as multilateral development banks, may restrict our ability to participate in projects, 
and could negatively impact our reputation and results of operations. 
5. We have had negative cash flows from operating activities in the certain past periods / fiscals and may 
continue to have negative cash flows in the future.
6. Our business has grown, including our revenue from operations that has grown at a CAGR of 10.56% 
from ₹6,574.95 million in Fiscal 2024 to ₹8,036.29 million in Fiscal 2026, and we may fail to manage

assure you that regulatory proceedings or actions will not be initiated against us in the future and we will 
not be subject to any penalty imposed by the competent regulatory authority in this regard.
8. Our Company is involved in certain legal proceedings. Any adverse decision in such proceedings may 
render us liable to liabilities / penalties and may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results 
of operations and cash flows. 
9. Our Subsidiaries, Hindustan Waste Treatment Private Limited, Vasudha Waste Treatment Private 
Limited, Fine Aeration Systems Private Limited and Pentagen Biofuels Private Limited, Sustainyx Smart 
Solution Private Limited (formerly Navitas Waste Treatment Private Limited) and SFC Umwelttechnik 
GmbH have availed unsecured loans from our Company that may be recalled at any time and the 
Subsidiaries may not have adequate funds to make timely payments or at all.
10. We have high working capital requirements, and may require additional financing to meet those 
requirements, which could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows and

65.19%, 63.51% and 39.94% for the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and Fiscals 2026, 2025 and
